headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: Mentat’s filesystem/network access can feed unstructured documents into third-party processing without strong verification or isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Mentat reads and writes files and shares state via filesystem, so unstructured can place attacker-controlled document content into a shared workspace that Mentat may later read as trusted input. unstructured also processes documents/images/text and writes files, making a file-based bridge plausible. This is not proven to be default instruction-following hijack, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF unstructured writes a document containing adversarial instructions into a directory Mentat later reads
IF Mentat is configured to treat file contents as authoritative task context
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct directories
Disable automatic ingestion of newly written files
Require manual review of document contents before Mentat reads them
Use read-only mounts for unstructured outputs
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between file producers and consumers

B_data_leakage.rationale: Mentat has broad network egress and handles model-provider API keys, while unstructured processes documents and images in a docker container with allowlisted egress. If both touch the same workspace, sensitive source code or documents can flow from one agent into the other’s outputs or remote calls. The profiles do not show a hard isolation boundary between them, so leakage is plausible in default use.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or document set
IF Mentat forwards file contents to its model provider during analysis
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of the shared workspace
Run unstructured on a separate input copy
Restrict Mentat to non-sensitive files only
Review outbound requests from Mentat before execution
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention rules

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem and read the filesystem, and Mentat explicitly shares state with other instances via filesystem while unstructured runs with docker but no stated locking. That creates a direct write-write conflict on shared paths, and Mentat also modifies git state, so concurrent edits can corrupt work or overwrite each other. The overlap is dangerous by default when co-located.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same directory or git repository
IF Mentat and unstructured run concurrently without external locking
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Pause one agent while the other writes
Commit or snapshot before switching agents
Use file locks around shared outputs
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Mentat produces diff-based edit proposals and unstructured transforms documents into extracted text, so one agent’s output can become the other’s input without a documented verification step. That makes extraction errors or malformed content propagate into code edits or downstream actions. The profiles do not show automatic execution of actions, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF Mentat consumes unstructured’s extracted text as authoritative context
IF extracted text contains omissions or hallucinated structure
mitigations: Require human review of extracted text before editing
Compare extracted output against source documents
Limit unstructured to non-critical documents
Use a second pass to verify key facts
requires-engineering: add validation between extraction and editing

E_compliance.rationale: Mentat’s docs show model-provider API calls and secrets handling, while unstructured’s docs show privacy-policy and docs endpoints plus docker isolation. No explicit residency, retention, or certification mismatch is documented, so only a low compliance concern is supportable. The other agent is not cited because the issue is not a cross-border or certification conflict proven by the profiles.
conditions: IF regulated data is sent through Mentat’s model-provider API
IF unstructured processes documents subject to stricter retention or residency rules
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in both tools
Review vendor privacy terms before use
Disable processing of sensitive documents
Store only minimal necessary outputs
requires-engineering: document and enforce retention/residency policy
